description: Walks the folder and records what is there: how many files and folders, their sizes, hidden files, links and timestamps. No file is opened. It then reads only what that walk stored to say whether the folder has a recognisable structure (a project, a dataset layout, an archive, backups) and how much changed since the previous walk. Cheap, and nothing is written into the folder. This definition is Resource Explorer's own walk and does not run Egeria's Folder Survey. If Egeria can read the folder, run Egeria's Folder Survey from the file system's folder-survey card instead; this definition's walk then stops and says so. A step that has not run shows "Not yet run", never an empty answer.

Walks the folder, then goes deeper. It profiles the columns of the tabular data files, reads README-style narrative files in full and indexes them for search inside Resource Explorer, and proposes matches between columns or file names and Egeria's data classes (proposals only; nothing is created in Egeria). It also reports which files nobody has touched for a long time, which files are duplicates, and who can read what (counts of owners, groups and modes, and secret-looking names that anyone can read). Costs more than scouting: it opens data and narrative files and hashes files to find duplicates. Nothing is written into the folder.
